copies.headline: CJ's Backfield Buries The League's Best Team
copies.body:
The running backs decided this one and it wasn't close. Chuba Hubbard went for 34.2, Jonathan Taylor added 12.3, and Ollie Gordon II chipped in 15.5 out of the flex — 62 points of ground game against Adam's Rico Dowdle and Kimani Vidal combining for 8.8. Adam won the QB spot by 21.7 with Brock Purdy and got 14.0 from the Colts against a Steelers defense that posted negative seven, and still lost by 12.2. That's how badly the backfield went.
The misses piled up. Sam LaPorta scored 2.6 on an 11.4 projection, Chris Olave 6.0 on 15.8, and Jalen Coker put up 0.3 in the flex while Antonio Williams sat on the bench with 12.2. CJ wasn't clean either — Tyler Shough gave him 10.0 while Deshaun Watson scored 21.4 in street clothes — but 118.3 was enough.
We had Adam by 21, which aged about as well as the LaPorta start. He's still 7-3 with the best all-play in the league at 78-32; CJ is 5-5 and still scoring eighth. One of these teams got away with something.

copies.headline: Logan's Flex and Defense Cost Him Again
copies.body:
The margin was 9.7 and you can find all of it in two lineup slots. Kaleb's Vikings D/ST put up 21.0 against Logan's Chiefs at 9.0, and Keenan Allen quietly turned in 11.1 at flex while Germie Bernard gave Logan exactly 1.0 point on a 10.9 projection. That's 22 points of swing from the two spots nobody drafts on purpose, and it erased a 33.2 from Joe Burrow and a 27.7 from Isaiah Likely at tight end.
Logan's problem wasn't the stars, it was everyone behind them. Tetairoa McMillan missed by 9.5, Jaylen Warren by 6.4, Bernard by 9.9 — roughly 26 points of shortfall from three starters while Kaleb got double digits from five of nine. We picked Logan by 17 and the top of his roster delivered on it; the bottom didn't show.
Logan falls to 4-6 with a 66-44 all-play and minus-two wins of luck, which is the statistical version of being haunted. Kaleb is 6-4 scoring 103.2 a game, 12th in the league, and it keeps working.

copies.headline: Noah's Patriots Stack Detonates in His Hands
copies.body:
The quarterback slot settled this before noon. Trevor Lawrence put up 26.8 for Christian, Drake Maye gave Noah 3.0 against a 22-point projection, and a 23.8-point hole at the single most predictable position is not something you dig out of with Josh Downs. Add the backfield — Chase Brown 28.3 and Bhayshul Tuten 20.3 against James Cook and a Rhamondre Stevenson who managed 1.5 on a 13.4 projection — and Christian was up 49 at two positions. Noah actually won WR and FLEX. It bought him nothing.
The New England experiment was the whole loss: Maye, Stevenson and Hunter Henry combined for 8.7 points, and Seth McGowan sat on the bench with 13.7. Christian left plenty behind too — Deebo Samuel's 25.9 rotting while Khalil Shakir mustered 7.5 — and still cleared 149.9.
We had Christian by 18; he tripled it. He's 5-5 with the third-best scoring average and a 70-40 all-play, which means the record is lying about him. Noah is 3-7, dead last in all-play, and the postseason assassin is running out of postseason to assassinate.

copies.headline: McCaffrey Buries John, Who Deserved Better
copies.body:
Christian McCaffrey put up 46.3 by himself, which is more than John got from his entire backfield plus his tight end. That's the game. Leif's running backs outscored John's 53.8 to 40.3, and the gap only looked that close because Emmett Johnson went for 35.1 in relief of the rest of John's roster. Kyren Williams managed 5.2 on an 18.6 projection, and when your RB1 misses by thirteen against a week where McCaffrey goes nuclear, there's no path.
John's receivers were the other wound: 13.0 combined, with DeMario Douglas turning a 10.0 projection into 1.4 while Xavier Hutchinson (15.8) and Malik Washington (13.4) sat. Flip that one slot and this is a John win. Leif had his own sins — Omar Cooper Jr. goose-egged, Kaelon Black's 14.6 rotted on the bench behind Woody Marks — and still won by 19.2.
Leif's 7-3 with the 6th-best scoring and a 52-58 all-play; he's +2.3 wins on luck and nobody's asking him to give them back. John falls to 5-5 scoring 130.1 a game, second in the league. We had Leif by nine.

copies.headline: Gibbs and Dak Bury Isaac's Giants
copies.body:
Mitchell won this in the backfield and never looked back. Jahmyr Gibbs put up 44.2 by himself — more than Isaac's entire running back room and flex combined — and Dak Prescott's 34.4 gave Mitchell a 14-point cushion at quarterback before anyone else touched the ball. Add DJ Moore's 19.4 in the flex against Wan'Dale Robinson's 4.0 and that's a 45-point swing across three slots. Isaac actually won four positions, including a 9-point D/ST edge, and it mattered not at all.
Isaac's problem was the supporting cast. Ja'Marr Chase went for 34.1 and Cam Skattebo added 27.2, but Malik Nabers (-8.7 vs projection), Javonte Williams (-7.1) and Robinson (-6.3) hollowed out the middle. Worse, Ryan Flournoy sat on the bench for 19.1 — start him over Robinson and this is a four-point game. Our preview had Mitchell by 7; he beat that by 11.
Mitchell is 3-7 with 149.0, which is the whole season: scoring like a contender, losing like a bottom-feeder. Isaac falls to 5-5 and is still chasing 2022.

copies.headline: Mahomes And A Kicker Bury Peter
copies.body:
Grant won this at the two spots nobody drafts for: quarterback and kicker. Patrick Mahomes put up 35.4 to Aaron Rodgers' 15.6, and Cam Little's 21.0 made Evan McPherson's 6.4 look like a typo. That's 34.4 points of edge from two roster slots, and it covered the 30.5 margin by itself. Tony Pollard's 23.9 and Amon-Ra St. Brown's 25.8 were just insurance.
Peter got the week of his life from George Pickens — 43.5 — and still lost by 30. That's the whole problem. Brock Bowers managed 3.8 on a 15.4 projection, A.J. Brown 4.7 on 12.5, and Denzel Boston 2.6 on 12.7 while Pat Freiermuth sat on the bench with 11.5. Three starters fell roughly 30 points short of their projections combined. No single Pickens game survives that.
Both sides now 5-5, but Grant's 118.3 per game and 57-53 all-play say he belongs there; Peter's 45-65 all-play and +0.9 luck say he doesn't. Three straight losses for the 2022 champ, and the preview had Grant by 13.

intro: Christian's 149.88 was the week's high mark, and it landed on Noah, who managed 91.42 and never got within shouting distance of a 58.5-point beating. Grant's 148.52 and Mitchell's 149.02 were nearly identical, but only one of them got to hang it on a team that scored 130 — Isaac lost by 18.7 and still outscored half the league. The closest call was Kaleb over Logan by 9.7, which is the kind of margin that turns one empty flex start into a week of staring at the ceiling.
